title: Approximate Quantum Error Correction at Chiral Topological Edges
authors: Yuntai Song, Zejun Liu, Zhencheng Wang, Jong Yeon Lee, Bowen Shi
abstract: Topologically ordered phases naturally realize quantum error correction through nonlocal encoding of quantum information. More recently, conformal field theories have been shown to realize approximate quantum error-correcting codes, but such constructions generally require fine tuning to criticality. Here we introduce a family of approximate quantum error-correcting codes realized by the chiral edges of two-dimensional topologically ordered phases. The proposed encoding combines the robustness of a gapped topological bulk with the flexibility of gapless edge conformal field theories. To characterize its robustness, we study coherent-information loss under local erasure. We derive an exact expression relating coherent-information loss to relative entropy, reducing the recoverability problem to universal properties of the edge theory. This leads to power-law scaling of coherent-information loss with the size of the erased region. We further show that, for geometrically local erasures near one edge, the two-dimensional chiral edge code is at least as robust as the dimensionally reduced CFT code, and is strictly more robust in several representative examples. For Abelian code subspaces, we further construct a power-law-range recovery map supported on the erased region together with a power-law-range buffer; this recovery map depends only on the code subspace, not on the unknown encoded state. We provide numerical calculations for lattice realizations of compact free boson and Ising CFT examples that support the theoretical predictions of the power-law exponents.
summary: This paper introduces and analyzes approximate quantum error correction codes realized by the chiral edges of 2D topologically ordered phases. By quantifying information loss using coherent information, the authors demonstrate that these 2D edge codes are highly robust, surpassing their simpler 1D CFT counterparts in resisting local errors. This advances the understanding of how topological protection can be harnessed for practical quantum computation.
main_problem: The goal is to develop and characterize Approximate Quantum Error Correction (AQEC) codes that leverage the inherent robustness of gapped topological phases while incorporating the flexibility provided by gapless edge conformal field theories.
main_result: The 2D chiral edge code was shown to be at least as robust against local erasures as its dimensionally reduced 1D CFT counterpart, exhibiting a quantifiable power-law scaling for information loss.
method: The analysis involves studying coherent-information loss under local erasure and deriving an exact relationship between this loss and relative entropy, reducing the problem to universal properties of the edge theory.
model_or_system: The study focuses on chiral edges arising from two-dimensional topologically ordered phases. These systems combine a gapped topological bulk with gapless edge conformal field theories (CFTs).
key_observables: Coherent-information loss ($\Delta(A; V)$), which quantifies logical information leaked to the erased region, and associated power-law scaling exponents.
important_parameters: The size of the erased region ($x$), the gap structure (gapped bulk vs. gapless edge), and the type of erasure (local).
main_assumptions: Key assumptions include dimensional reduction relating 2D diagnostics to 1D CFT properties, and relying on topological-sector orthogonality for mathematical simplification.
figures_summary: Figure 1 summarizes results comparing coherent information loss between the 2D chiral edge code and the 1D CFT code; Figure 2 illustrates the definition of $\Delta(A; V)$ in terms of system regions.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by establishing the physical model (chiral edges), developing the diagnostic tool ($\Delta$ via relative entropy), deriving scaling laws, proving the robustness hierarchy ($\gamma \geq \alpha$), and finally constructing a power-law recovery map for Abelian subspaces.
why_interesting: This work provides concrete theoretical tools to assess error resilience in exotic quantum states found at boundaries of topological materials, linking bulk topology directly to information processing capabilities.
